modes.name: bad_catalog_data_presented_as_fact
modes.definition: Fail if the reply answers a product question with a value taken from invalid or ambiguous catalog data (a negative or otherwise impossible price, or several products sharing the requested title) without telling the user the data is invalid or ambiguous. Pass if the reply flags the problem and does not turn it into a definite answer (or asks which product is meant).
modes.boundary: Covers catalog (product) data only. A mismatch between order and product records is record_inconsistency_not_flagged. Flagging the problem and then still giving the cleaned-up value (support-0129) counts as Fail.
modes.evaluator: code check (negative price or duplicate titles in the search_products result, compared with the reply) plus LLM judge for whether it was flagged
modes.open_question: Split into invalid_price and duplicate_title if the fixes differ (sanitising prices vs disambiguating products).

modes.name: record_inconsistency_not_flagged
modes.definition: Fail if the order record contradicts other records or the user's description (e.g. the order's store differs from the store that owns the product) and the agent states the record as fact or invents an explanation instead of flagging the inconsistency and escalating. Pass if it flags or escalates.
modes.boundary: Order or account records, not catalog search results (that is bad_catalog_data_presented_as_fact). Applies only when the mismatch is detectable from data the user or the tools provided.
modes.evaluator: LLM judge (needs to compare the order with product ownership); a code check can pre-filter known data-quality cases
modes.open_question: Only 2 positives (0068 weaker: nobody flagged it). The depth search should look for more, and for close negatives.

modes.name: store_return_window_not_verified
modes.definition: Fail if the agent states, assumes or relies on a return window (or a reason for ineligibility) without checking whether the store has its own window, when the store's policy differs or the user asserts a window. Pass if it checks the store policy, or the store has no override and the platform window is stated correctly.
modes.boundary: About which window applies, not about date arithmetic. Not checking when no override exists and the stated deadline is right (support-0137) is a close negative under the current wording; support-0027 is borderline because it hands the check to the user.
modes.spec_id: SPEC gap (no requirement to verify a store override); related to cw-store-overrides and RESP-3
modes.evaluator: code check (store override exists and the agent made no get_policy or store-policy lookup) plus LLM judge for the stated window
modes.open_question: Requires a SPEC revision before an evaluator: decide whether the agent must always verify a store override before stating a deadline or eligibility.

modes.name: write_outcome_overstated
modes.definition: Fail if the reply describes a write action (refund, cancellation, escalation) or its consequences as more complete or certain than the most recent tool result supports, e.g. 'Done' or 'will be approved' for queued_for_approval, or side effects no tool reported. Pass if the reply matches the tool status.
modes.boundary: Requires a write tool call or a promise about one. Invented options that were never acted on are unsupported_option_offered.
modes.evaluator: code check (tool status vs completion words in the reply) plus LLM judge for promised consequences
modes.open_question: Only 1 clear positive. Depth search: issue_refund with queued_for_approval, and cancel/escalate replies.

modes.name: unsupported_option_offered
modes.definition: Fail if the reply offers the user an option, remedy, exception or process that no policy or tool result supports (e.g. 'refuse delivery', 'a human may make an exception', 'support will help you update your card'). Pass if every offered option is backed by a policy or tool.
modes.boundary: About invented paths forward. A wrong claim about a completed write is write_outcome_overstated. Offering escalation itself is supported (cw-escalations); claiming what the human will grant is not.
modes.spec_id: RESP-3; RESP-5 (partly SPEC gap: no explicit 'no invented remedies' rule)
modes.evaluator: LLM judge with the policy corpus
modes.open_question: Mostly borderline. support-0225 also exposes the SCOPE-2 vs ESC-2 conflict (record a SPEC revision).

modes.name: policy_claim_not_cited
modes.definition: Fail if the reply makes a claim derived from a policy document (return window, cancellation rule, dispute handling) without citing the policy id. Pass if every policy-derived claim cites its id.
modes.boundary: Citation only; whether the claim is correct belongs to the other modes. Rule-based, so it can be checked on every trace.
modes.evaluator: code check (policy-topic keywords vs cw-/store- ids in the reply) plus LLM judge for edge cases
modes.open_question: Never the first failure in batch 1, only a secondary remark, so there are no open codes of its own yet. Keep it only if structured labeling shows it matters.

spec_revisions_to_consider.topic: SCOPE-2 (refuse card changes) vs ESC-2 (account changes go to a human)

modes.name: inconsistent_record_presented_as_valid
modes.origin: axial round 1 after batch 1, proposed by agent, approved by student
modes.definition: Fail if the agent states, or explains away, tool data that is invalid or internally inconsistent (e.g. a negative price, or an order whose store differs from the store that owns the product) instead of flagging it. Pass if it flags the inconsistency or escalates.
modes.product_change: Flag invalid or inconsistent data to the user and escalate instead of answering from it.
modes.boundary: vs ambiguous_match_treated_as_unique: here the data itself is wrong; there the data is valid but several records match.
modes.evaluator: LLM judge (possibly code-assisted: negative prices, known data-quality cases)

modes.name: ambiguous_match_treated_as_unique
modes.origin: axial round 1 after batch 1, proposed by agent, approved by student
modes.definition: Fail if several records match the user's description and the agent answers about one of them without asking which one or listing them. Pass if it lists the matches or asks.

modes.boundary: vs inconsistent_record_presented_as_valid: the matching records are valid; the problem is choosing one silently.
modes.evaluator: code check possible (tool result count > 1) plus LLM judge

modes.definition: Fail if the reply makes a claim derived from a policy document without citing its policy id. Facts restated from a tool result (e.g. the issue_refund note '5 to 10 business days') are not policy claims. Pass if every policy-derived claim cites its id.
modes.product_change: Always attach the policy id to policy-derived statements.
modes.boundary: Citation only; whether the claim is correct belongs to the other modes.
modes.evaluator: LLM judge (code can check for policy ids)
modes.round2_note: No batch-2 additions: 0173 was rejected; no accepted batch-2 note has a missing citation as its first failure (missing cites appear only as secondary remarks in 0002, 0086, 0199, 0238).
modes.revision_note: Round 3: excluded facts restated from tool results (support-0004). Minor uncited asides next to a cited main claim are a Pass (consistent with support-0173 and support-0018).

modes.name: invented_process_or_exception
modes.origin: axial round 2 after batch 2, proposed by agent, approved by student
modes.definition: Fail if the reply offers an exception, procedure, team, document requirement, remedy or timeline that is not present in any tool result or policy. Pass if every offered path and timeline is backed by a tool result or policy.
modes.product_change: Restrict remedies and procedures to those in the policy corpus and tool results; otherwise say so or escalate without promising.
modes.boundary: vs policy_claim_uncited: there the policy exists but is not cited; here the described thing does not exist.
modes.evaluator: LLM judge with the policy corpus
modes.revision_note: Round 3: timelines added explicitly (support-0017 '24–48 hours'; support-0140 '1–2 business days' as a secondary example). Round 3b: criteria-drift re-check added 0012, 0026, 0151, 0221 as secondary positives (their first-failure codes stay in their original modes; 0221 previously had no mode).

modes.name: scope_escalation_unclear
modes.origin: axial round 1 after batch 1, proposed by agent, approved by student
modes.definition: Pending SPEC decision: the agent's handling of a request SPEC both refuses (SCOPE-2) and routes to a human (ESC-2) is unclear or promises an outcome.
modes.product_change: Revise SPEC to resolve SCOPE-2 vs ESC-2, then update the prompt.
modes.boundary: Needs a SPEC revision before it can become final.
modes.evaluator: undecided (after the SPEC revision)
modes.dissolved_reason: Resolved by the SPEC revision (ESC-2, 2026-11-10): payment-card changes are account changes; refuse card details and escalate. support-0225 is correct behavior under the revised SCOPE-2/ESC-2 (annotation revised to no failure); support-0012's first failure stays under policy_claim_uncited.

resolved_questions: Consistency 0027 vs 0137: resolved by student, both are store_return_window_not_verified (0137 open code revised, original kept in history).
Possible 7th group: created as invented_process_or_exception in round 2 (0002, 0086, 0095, 0238, 0109, 0168).

spec_revisions.change: Payment-card changes count as account changes: refuse card details (SCOPE-2) and offer escalation (ESC-2).

modes.name: unreliable_tool_data_presented_as_fact
modes.origin: axial round 2 after batch 2, proposed by agent, approved by student
modes.definition: Fail if the reply presents tool output that is invalid, internally inconsistent, empty or the result of a malformed call as a reliable fact (or explains it away) instead of flagging it or escalating. Pass if it flags the problem or escalates.
modes.product_change: Validate tool output and say when it is empty, invalid or anomalous; escalate inconsistencies.
modes.boundary: vs ambiguous_match_treated_as_unique: here the data is wrong, empty or anomalous; there the data is valid but several records match. vs invented_process_or_exception: here the agent misreports what a tool returned; there it describes things no tool or policy contains.
modes.evaluator: LLM judge (possibly code-assisted: negative prices, known data-quality cases)
modes.merge_note: 0181 (empty result from malformed '*' search) merged here: same product change (validate tool output, say when empty or anomalous)
modes.revision_note: Round 3: depth search confirmed the 'empty result from a poor query' sub-pattern (0025, 0090; same as 0181). No definition change.
modes.round4_note: Final uniform batch: 0132 (store mismatch), 0187 (deadline computed from the order date with delivered_at missing), 0008 (borderline: reversed dates restated). 0006 added as a close negative (missing delivery date flagged, no deadline computed).

modes.name: ambiguous_match_treated_as_unique
modes.origin: axial round 1 after batch 1, proposed by agent, approved by student
modes.definition: Fail if several records match the user's description and the agent answers about one of them without asking which one or listing them. Pass if it lists the matches or asks.
modes.product_change: Ask a clarifying question (or list the matches) when a lookup returns more than one candidate.
modes.boundary: vs inconsistent_record_presented_as_valid: the matching records are valid; the problem is choosing one silently.
modes.evaluator: code check possible (tool result count > 1) plus LLM judge
modes.open_question: Target in the depth batch; drop if fewer than 3 positives.
modes.rejected_reason: Depth search over all 290 unbatched traces found 9 duplicate-title hits; the 5 reviewed (0021, 0060, 0108, 0169, 0184) all listed the matches, asked, or used the product id. Only 1 positive (support-0022) remains, under the 3-positive minimum, so the mode is dropped. Record kept; 0022 stays as an observation.
modes.origin_rejection: round 3 after depth batch, proposed by agent, applied at student's request (2026-11-10)

modes.name: store_return_window_not_verified
modes.origin: axial round 1 after batch 1, proposed by agent, approved by student
modes.definition: Fail if the agent states a return window, a deadline or a reason for (in)eligibility without checking the store's own policy (a store-policy lookup or citation). This applies even when the stated date happens to be correct. Pass if it checks the store policy, or if it states no window, deadline or reason and relies only on the eligibility flag.
modes.product_change: Look up the store policy before stating a window, or have a tool return the effective window.
modes.boundary: About which window applies, not date arithmetic. Not verifying the store policy counts as Fail even when the stated date happens to be correct (student decision on support-0137, axial round 1).
modes.spec_id: SPEC gap (no requirement to verify a store override)
modes.evaluator: code check (store-policy lookup before stating a deadline) or LLM judge
modes.revision_note: Round 3: (a) Pass when no window/deadline/reason is stated and the eligibility flag is used (support-0035, Northwind refund at day 34 of 45). (b) Search signal fixed: get_policy(cw-returns) is not a store-policy check (support-0014 was mis-flagged as a close negative).

modes.name: write_outcome_overstated
modes.origin: axial round 1 after batch 1, proposed by agent, approved by student
modes.definition: Fail if the reply states or implies that a write action is complete, approved or certain beyond the latest tool result (e.g. a human 'will approve/finalize/process it'), or promises the outcome of a write that was never performed. Pass if it reports the tool status accurately; acknowledging a submission ('Done — queued for approval') with the correct status is a Pass.
modes.product_change: Report write results exactly as the tool status gives them (queued vs approved), with no promised side effects.
modes.boundary: Requires a write action or a promise about one; invented options without a write fall outside this mode.
modes.evaluator: code check plus LLM judge
modes.revision_note: Round 3: added 'promises the outcome of a write that was never performed' (support-0010: escalated instead of issue_refund, then 'will approve your refund'). Clarified that 'Done' plus an accurate queued status is a Pass (support-0017); invented timelines move to invented_process_or_exception.
modes.round4_note: 0100: 'Done.' plus an accurate escalation status, a close negative under the round-3 rule.
